# okfctl

> A command-line tool for authoring and maintaining Open Knowledge Format (OKF)
> bundles. It ships as one static binary for macOS, Linux, and Windows: put it
> on your PATH and it runs. okfctl does not author
> the OKF specification; it is a conformant consumer that enforces the spec floor
> and keeps anything stricter behind an explicit opt-in overlay.

okfctl scaffolds a bundle, adds and moves nodes without breaking links, keeps the
reserved `index.md`/`log.md` files current, checks a corpus against the spec, and
reports on its health and link graph.

## Docs

- [Command reference](https://okfctl.dev/reference/commands/): Every command, its flags, and a runnable example—generated from and kept in sync with the binary.
- [Concepts](https://okfctl.dev/concepts/): Bundles, nodes, the link graph, and the reserved files.
- [Authoring a bundle](https://okfctl.dev/guides/authoring/): From an empty directory to a validated bundle.
- [Curation health](https://okfctl.dev/guides/curation-health/): Using `lint`, `analyze`, and `--strict` in CI.
- [Migrating to OKF v0.3](https://okfctl.dev/guides/migrating/): The two-phase `migrate` plan and apply for v0.1 and v0.2 bundles.

## Specification

- [Open Knowledge Format spec (SPEC.md)](https://github.com/open-knowledge-format/open-knowledge-format/blob/main/SPEC.md): The authoritative OKF specification (v0.3), maintained in `open-knowledge-format/open-knowledge-format`. The former `GoogleCloudPlatform/open-knowledge-format` repo is deprecated and frozen at v0.2. Where the spec defines behavior, the spec wins.

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/cwest/okfctl): Source, releases, and issues.
